caption: New wind-combed procedural grass meadow at noon in Harrowmere Vale; bare ground between clumps is still flat grey-brown and the distant hills float as disconnected ribbons in the fog.
Grass on a Vale slope at 16:30 golden hour reads well up close, but past the 64 m grass radius the valley is an empty brown plane under grey sky with no trees, rocks or village.
Noon in Harrowmere Vale: the hill bowl finally renders solid behind the wind-combed meadow (terrain winding fix); still no trees, rocks, village or textures, and the capsule player is a speck.
16:30: long hill shadows sweep across the valley, but the shadowed foreground is crushed to black and the sky is flat grey.
22:30: new moonlight and star field make the night readable on wind-bent grass; no moon disc, fireflies or night life yet.
New procedural black-oak grove backlit at 15:30 with long trunk shadows through the grass; foreground shadow is crushed to black and leaf cards read as blobs up close.
Oak woodland now crowns the vale's hills above the wind-blown meadow at noon; boulders are too small to read, sky is flat and the hill ground is still bare procedural brown.
Backlit oak grove at 15:30: the shadowed grass and trunks now read with cool skylight instead of crushing to black; leaf cards still look like flat blobs up close.
Noon meadow and oak-crowned hills: shade under the grass is readable now; boulders are too small, hill ground is bare procedural brown.
Village edge at 16:30, previously half black: the shadowed meadow is now visible, but the sky is too dark navy for late afternoon and the horizon is empty.
16:30 over the village meadow: the sky is now a deep clear blue instead of navy and the shaded meadow reads; a tree trunk still blocks the left edge and the hills are bare procedural orange.
Noon oak slope under a bright blue sky with readable shadow sides; leaf cards are blobby up close and the valley floor is bare brown.
Noon meadow with oak groves and, new, a hazy snow-capped mountain ring closing the horizon; ridgelines are still faceted at distance and the hills are bare brown.
Late-afternoon view across the vale to layered ranges and snowy peaks; the foreground grass sits in deep shadow and the peaks form a uniform sawtooth.
A rook flock feeding on cropped turf in the vale at 14:00; reads as a real field, but the crop patch shows bare brown ground and the birds are tiny at 15 m.
Rooks bursting up out of the meadow as the camera comes within 10 m; motion reads in a clip, but the still is small dark specks and the shaded hillside is muddy.
The player is now a rigged, animated human instead of a capsule, standing in the afternoon meadow; still wrong: sci-fi armour and visor instead of a mythic hero, no face, hair or staff.
Follow camera on the player mid-stride in the idle/walk/run blend at dusk, lantern glow on the grass; still wrong: placeholder Mixamo soldier model and no foot IK.

Close rear view of the hero's new procedural staff slung across the back: worn bronze caps, red lacquered shaft, hemp-wrapped grip; still wrong: it is strapped to a sci-fi armoured soldier with no strap or scabbard holding it.
The hero seen from behind against a low sun, staff diagonal across the back at body scale; still wrong: placeholder Mixamo soldier model, flat cartoonish far mountains.
Overhead-slam wind-up: both hands IK-locked on the staff raised over the head, chest twisted into the swing; still wrong: sci-fi soldier model, legs stay in idle, harsh red ground under the grass.
Mid-sweep of the light string with a faint pale swing trail; still wrong: the two-handed grip reads like holding a rifle at this angle, trail too faint, placeholder soldier model.

Overhead slam frozen 5 ticks after it lands on the practice post's iron-capped top: dust burst, flying chaff and the swing arc read as a hit; still wrong: placeholder sci-fi soldier, dust a little too bright, tall grass hides the feet.
Opening sweep connecting with the straw-bound oak practice post; still wrong: the chaff is too small to read at this distance and the staff is hidden behind the body, placeholder model.
Close look at the new practice post (weathered oak, straw bundle, hemp lashings, rusted iron band) backlit at 10 h; straw and rope read well, the shaded oak top goes near-black and looks too smooth.

The new dash-step dodge frozen early: the hero sinks low and leans hard into the dash past the practice post, vitality bar with its pale lost segment bottom-left; still the sci-fi placeholder model and no real roll clip.

Later in the dodge with the reworked HUD: thin red vitality bar over a pale-gold stamina bar, both readable over bright grass; the pose reads as a running lean rather than a Wukong dodge, and the model is a placeholder.

Hollow Soldier at the peak of its wind-up: grey ash-stone body with the ember flaring in the chest and a glint on the spear blade as the tell; still fails — the sci-fi armour silhouette shows under the ash and the backlit foreground grass is blown out.

Side-on as the soldier's lunging thrust lands on the hero at the practice post; the thrust reads as a body lunge but the spear is hidden along the view line, and both models are placeholder sci-fi soldiers.

Lock-on: the follow camera slides over the right shoulder to frame the hero and the Hollow Soldier mid wind-up, with the bone-white reticle on its chest; still wrong: sci-fi placeholder bodies, over-bright foreground grass, steep framing shows too much ground.

Parry: the hero raises the staff into the heavy just as the Hollow Soldier's thrust lands, a spark burst throws the spear aside; still wrong: sci-fi placeholder bodies, the spark reads as a soft orange blob, foreground grass blades are flat and glaring.

Tier-2 heavy smash driving the staff into the meadow; still wrong: the slam dust is a grey sphere, a stray glint cloud hangs in the sky, the staggered soldier is missing from the frame (shot tool), placeholder hero body.

First light sweep connecting with the practice post: the staff now travels flat at shoulder height as authored instead of lying sideways; still wrong: placeholder sci-fi hero body, the post blocks the hero in this camera, bare red soil between grass clumps.
Overhead strike coming down on the centre line with a long grip (vertical trail behind the post); still wrong: camera puts the post in front of the hero, placeholder body, flat foreground grass.
Hollow Soldier coiling its new sweep: spear wound flat behind its right side, chest ember flaring; still placeholder sci-fi bodies and faceted far ridges.
The sweep mid-arc cutting flat through the hero at waist height; no spear swing trail yet, bodies are still the sci-fi placeholder.

Night meadow at 21:30: fireflies drift and blink over the grass, the brightest few lighting the blades green around them; the hero is still the sci-fi placeholder and the far ridges glow brighter than the night sky.
Low evening sun through the oak grove with a midge swarm glinting beside the trunk; the glints are subtle (a few px), canopy leaf cards are still large and flat.

Night meadow at 22:00 with fireflies: the moonlit haze now continues into the sky so the far ridges sit as soft layered silhouettes under the stars instead of a glowing blue cut-out; ridges are still faceted and the grass blades read coarse up close.

Hero by the practice post at 21:30, lit only by the moon and fireflies now that the sourceless orange 'lantern' pool is gone; the hero is still the sci-fi placeholder and the tree canopies blow out under the moon haze.

18:12, looking west over the meadow: the sky now holds a warm afterglow behind the silhouetted ridges after sunset instead of going black; the ridges are still faceted and the foreground grass is near-black.
18:36 blue hour: the glow cools to violet-blue over the horizon as stars appear; the stars switch on all at once, too dense and gold-tinted for this early in the dusk.

18:24 toward the sunset: afterglow behind the peaks under a violet sky, and the meadow and oaks now lit by the twilight instead of black; the valley floor is too saturated rose-red and the canopies are still leaf cards.
17:45 toward the sun: the low sun now lights the meadow a warm gold instead of an orange-red wash, with long oak shadows; still fails on faceted far ridges and leaf-card canopies.
18:24 twilight: the valley floor now sits in a dusty mauve afterglow instead of saturated rose-red, ridges layered in haze; fails on faceted ridges, near-black canopies and coarse foreground grass.
Hero rocks back from a spear thrust that broke the heavy charge, staff thrown wide, impact dust; the soldier is missing from the frame (known shot bug), hero small in frame, ridges still faceted.
Pre-dawn at 5.6 h: mauve glow behind the eastern ridges, mist in the oak valley, blue sky to the west; a dark rock edge clips the left of frame and ridges are faceted.
The hero 0.6 s after a killing blow, knees buckled with the staff still gripped low; framed far left, soldier missing from the frame (shot bug), Vanguard armour and faceted ridges.
The fallen hero lying face-down in the amber grass before the screen fades to black; reads as a body, but the pose is a rigid plank and the sci-fi armour is still the model.

Half a second after a killing blow the hero's knees fold onto the grass (bone-level bend, legs no longer sink into the ground), chest curled, one arm out; still the sci-fi Vanguard armour, coarse near grass.
The hero lying face-down with legs extended and head turned, staff dropped in the grass; reads as a fallen body, but the grass does not flatten under it and the armour is not mythic.

The Hollow Soldier now wears a deep hood with a dark face void, a ragged shoulder mantle, a sash and a torn tabard to the knees, the ember glowing through the open chest; the silhouette reads as a cloaked revenant, but it is backlit and the legs still show the old armour greaves.
Side view of the rags in daylight: woven hemp hood, mantle and sash over the ash body; the cloth is still a uniform charcoal and the tabards hang stiff as boards rather than draping.

Close look at the Hollow Soldier's legs (grass hidden): the old greaves are now bound in wound hemp bandages fitted to the armour, but the wraps still read bulky and barrel-shaped and the boots show below.

Side view in daylight: hood, mantle, sash and the new shin wraps hide most of the sci-fi armour; the shins look padded rather than bound and the ember cracks on the thighs still read as armour plates.
Hollow Soldier legs now bound in hemp: thigh, shin and boot wraps hide the old armour; the wraps are too thick and the boot wrap is a lump.
Side view of the Hollow Soldier in the meadow: hood, mantle, tabards and bandaged limbs read as one revenant, but the silhouette is padded and bulky.

Macro shot with depth of field of a small tortoiseshell basking on the meadow at 11 h; reads as a butterfly, but it hovers on no grass stem, its pattern washes out in the warm grade, and the near grass blades are flat ribbons over bare brown soil.
A peacock butterfly settled over the 14 h meadow from half a metre; too small to read its eyes at this range, and the clumped grass over bare brown ground looks like a prototype.
A buttercup drift speckles the 10:30 meadow with yellow heads above the wind-bent grass; the black soil under the grass and flat blade ribbons still look like a prototype.
Knapweed, ox-eye daisies and yarrow mixed through the 15 h meadow beside the hero and the Hollow Soldier; flowers read, but bare brown soil between grass clumps dominates.
A small tortoiseshell settled on a yarrow umbel (perching on real flowers now, not air); the umbel was too sparse here and was densified after, and the ground is black.

Knee-height across a buttercup drift: the ground between the clumps is now lit turf with lying blades instead of a black void; the blade stroke pattern repeats like tread plate at grazing angles and the grass ribbons are still flat.
Looking down at the meadow floor: straw-strewn sward, moss and clover between the clumps reads as real ground; clump shadows are still very dark and the clumps too regular.
Afternoon valley from a hillside: the turf floor holds up at distance with no shimmer; the backlit tree crowns blow out white and the far peaks are faceted.
A rain front over the valley at noon: grey overcast light, rain streaks, wind-combed grass, the far ridges lost in rain haze; the sky is a flat grey with no cloud forms and the ridges are faceted.
The hero in the meadow in the rain: soaked, darkened grass bent by gusts and streaks falling; the hero is still the sci-fi placeholder and no splashes or puddles show on the ground.

Clear noon over the Vale with the new cloud deck: cumulus with sunlit tops and grey shadowed bellies drift over the ridges instead of an empty sky; the oak crowns are still blobby cards and the ridges faceted.

A rain front from the valley: one grey ceiling meeting the ridges in rain haze, wind-combed grass, streaks; the deck is too uniform (no rolling bellies or scud) and the far ridges still read as a dark cut-out.

Late afternoon toward the sun: rose-lit cumulus and streaks over the low sun, long tree shadows on the meadow; the trees are still blobby silhouettes and the cloud colour is a little too pink overhead.

A rain pool in a meadow hollow: raindrop rings across the water, tufts standing in it and mirrored by SSR at the far shore; the near water is very dark, the shoreline is hard and the grass cards still read flat.
The same pool before the ripple pass: SSR mirrors the far tufts and the sky sheen brightens toward the far bank under a grey rain haze; the meadow beyond is dim and flat.

Cumulus shadows now drift over the Vale at 15 h: the far valley glows gold in a sun gap while the right-hand foothills sit in cloud shade; tree crowns still read as flat leaf cards and the far peaks are smooth and faceted.

Looking down the valley at 14 h with sunlit and cloud-shaded patches across the meadow and mountains; the leaf cards facing the sun blow out to white like blossom, and the haze toward the sun washes out the right half.

Looking down the valley toward the sun at 14 h: the oak crowns now read olive-green with sunlit tops instead of white blossom; the haze toward the sun still washes out the right half and the far peaks are faceted.

An oak at 15 h above the sunlit Vale, leaves now deep olive with a rare brown dead leaf instead of apple-like rust blobs; the leaf cards are still oversized at close range and the crowns lack fine silhouette detail.

The hero runs through a rain-filled meadow pool: raindrop rings on the water and small splash crowns speckling the grass and pool; the foot splash at the hero's stride is too small to read and the hero is still the sci-fi Vanguard stand-in.
Low view over a wind-combed pool in a downpour (before the drop splashes were fixed): rain rings, streaks and grey haze read as real weather; grass blades are still flat ribbons up close.

After a shower the hero runs through a pool: ring trains spread across the water behind each footfall and a white crown bursts at the foot; the hero is still the sci-fi Vanguard, the splash sheet reads as a white sickle and the grass is flat ribbons.
Downpour over a meadow pool: bigger foot splash at the hero's stride, rain rings everywhere; placeholder hero and low-detail grass keep it short of Wukong.

Night storm over the Vale: a jagged bolt drops from the flash-lit deck and the meadow flares blue-white; the bolt's foot gets a dark outline against the mountains, and the faceted mountain ring and ribbon grass still read as prototype.
Afternoon downpour with a bolt striking past the oak groves through the rain haze; atmosphere works, but the hills and grass lack Wukong-level detail.
Night storm, sheet lightning: the rain deck glows from inside behind the ridge with no channel, the meadow faintly lit; the ridges are faceted cut-outs and the rain streaks barely show.
Rain at 13:00 with the hero still dry: grey downpour, wind-bent grass; the hero is still the sci-fi Vanguard stand-in and the grass is ribbons, so not a Wukong shot.
Same moment with the hero soaked: suit and staff grip darker and glossier, clearly wet; no drips or rivulets yet and the hero model is still the stand-in.

The hero sheltering under an oak in a downpour: rain stops under the crown and the ground beneath stays drier; still fails because the leaf cards read as big flat blobs and the grass as yellow spikes.
Open meadow in the same storm: pools, raindrop rings and wet soil unchanged outside the crowns; the wet bank top right is close to blown out and the far valley is a flat grey veil.
Hero under an oak in a downpour, fog over the far groves; the canopy drips do not read in a still frame here, ridges and the hero model are still not Wukong-grade.
After the shower the oak crown still sheds sparse drops in a low warm sun; the drops read only as tiny beads, the shaded hero is near black and the ground under the tree is flat.
Far mountain ring from the south-east ridge: domain-warped peaks with per-pixel gullies and crags instead of flat facets; still hazy grey and the near oaks are blobby.
Dusk toward the evening sun: snow lies in the new erosion gullies of the far peaks; foreground is too dark and the meadow shows banded shadow stripes.
After a shower the drenched hero sheds drops off hands, knees and the staff end (bright beads by the feet); the dull grey dusk, plastic sci-fi suit and hazy grey backdrop still fail the Wukong bar.

Sunset over the snow peaks as the rook flocks stream toward their roost (the dark specks upper left); the camera sits below the hill crest so the rookery itself is hidden, and the grass and oaks read dark and blobby.

Inside the rookery grove just after sunset with the rooks settled in the crowns; the warm sky and backlit grass have mood, but the perched birds are lost in the black crowns and the oaks are blobby silhouettes.

The meadow at 21.5 h under the new night grade: moonlit blue-grey grass, fireflies and starlit peaks now read like night instead of a gold-lit field; still too flat and grey, the sky lost its blue and the left-edge rock is a black wedge.
The valley at 10.5 h with the new film grade (warm highlights, cool shadows, grain, vignette): a convincing amber late-morning mood; oak crowns are still blobby and the near grass carpet reads noisy.

New ruined watchtower on the spur west of the village: a broken round keep and a robbed-out curtain wall of chipped cut stone stand on the skyline; half backlit from the low camera, the stone reads dark and the left grass blows out white.

Standing in the breach of the watchtower at 13.5 h: coursed ashlar with worn arrises and the vale beyond, but the shaded inner face is near black (no bounce light reaches it) so the stonework barely reads.
The watchtower ruin from up the slope with the sun behind: lit, readable sandstone keep over the vale; the courses are still too regular and brick-like.
Inside the keep: the shaded inner face now reads as coursed stone thanks to bounce fill and grass is off the floor; the floor and rubble tops are still near black.

Inside the ruined keep at 13:30: rubble now reads as pale sandstone with moss on its tops and the inner wall is lit by the bounce fill, but the earth floor between the stones is still near black and the courses are too regular.
The watchtower ruin on its knoll under a cumulus sky with the vale and mountains behind; believable, but the block courses are brick-regular and the far range reads hazy grey.
16 h looking toward the low sun: oak crowns now glow yellow-green with transmitted light over a sunlit meadow instead of black silhouettes; leaf cards still read as a few oversized leaves up close.
16 h: the watchtower knoll is in sun now that the mountain ring no longer shadows the vale; the keep's courses are still brick-regular same-size blocks.
16 h front-lit hill: oaks lit and readable, but the low camera sees mostly the dark lower blades of the near grass, so the foreground is still too dark.

Fern drift under the oaks at 13 h: shuttlecock ferns with arching pinnate fronds now fill the grove floor and the meadow grass thins under the crowns; the woodland shade is still near black and the ferns lack fine silhouette detail up close.
Grove edge at 10.5 h with the new understory: sunlit fern clumps and thinned shade grass on the right; ferns in the deep shade on the left vanish into a near-black floor.

The oak grove floor at 13 h: a lit carpet of fallen tan and russet oak leaves under the crowns with green ferns, no longer black; the leaf bed is still a bit grid-regular and close fern fronds show moire.

The afternoon meadow behind the hero: grass along the 18 m track the hero walked is combed over toward him and springs back at the far end; the track is still subtle (no clear lane or blade backs) and the grass near the camera is dark at the roots.

The hero's track through the afternoon meadow now reads as a laid-flat lane with boot prints pressed along it; the ground in the lane is still near black (the standing grass shadows it) and the prints barely show in turf.
The same track after rain: boot prints should hold water, but only a glint or two shows through the grass and the lane is less clear than in the dry shot.

A herd of procedural red deer hinds and calves grazing the amber meadow at 16.5 h; they read as deer and the scene feels alive, but at 19 m they are small dark silhouettes with little coat detail and the foreground grass is dark.

Model check of the new procedural red deer: standing, walking, grazing and galloping poses; good silhouette and coat markings, but the head is long and thin and the upper legs join the body as plain columns.
Red deer grazing the meadow at 10 h, now lit by the meadow bounce with a readable red coat and cream rumps; the near grass is still sparse tufts over bare dark soil and the oaks read stylized.
The herd at 16.5 h with the reworked head, neck and legs grazing below the oak line; deer still small in frame and the foreground grass is dark.
The deer meadow at 10 h with the new short sward: the bare dark soil between the tall clumps is now a green under-layer; the tall clumps still read as spiky regular tufts and the oaks look stylized.
Behind the hero at 11 h: the meadow floor reads as continuous grass to ~25 m instead of tufts over soil; the hero is still the sci-fi Vanguard and the practice post crowds the frame.

Midday meadow round the hero: tall grass is now a mix of arching leafy clumps and low tussocks in knots over the short sward instead of one repeated spiky fan; hero is still the sci-fi Vanguard and the practice post crowds the frame.
Evening over the valley: seeding grass stems with straw panicles catch the low sun on the slope in front; the far mountain ring is still a pale, smooth, blobby silhouette and the oaks are stylized.

The hero now reads as a mythic wanderer: woven straw hat over an indigo hood, dark mantle, madder robe panels, ochre sash and linen bindings; still the Vanguard visor under the hat, no face, and the practice post crowds the frame.
The hero's sci-fi plates now read as dark lacquered lamellar and the blue visor is gone under a dark face cloth; the face is still a dark void with no eyes and the practice post crowds the frame.
Close rear view: straw hat, indigo hood and staff read well, but the mantle is a flat brown slab with a hard hem and the new face shot framed the hero's back.

Rear view in the meadow: the hero's mantle now falls in folds to a soft scalloped hem over the madder robe and slung staff; the folds still read faintly at this range and the practice post crowds the frame.
The face shot now frames the hero from the front-left under the straw hat, but the face is still a black void of hood and face cloth in the brim's shade with no eyes or skin.

The hero now has a face: skin, brows and two dark eyes look out between the hood and the indigo face cloth under the straw hat; still a smooth doll-like shell with no nose or cheek shape, and the eyes never blink.
A soft face fill now lifts the hood and face cloth out of the brim's black shade, but from a camera at eye height the brim and down-pitched head still hide the eyes.

Front view of the hero with the straw hat now pushed back: the eyes show clearly under a brim whose underside no longer glows, but the face reads cartoonish (wide bright sclera, orange skin, no nose or cheek shape) and the hood and mantle are a flat dark mass.
A deer path trodden through the meadow grass with hoof prints pressed into it; the laid lane reads, but the 8 cm cloven slots are lost in the dark soil and grass at 3 m.
Deer tracks beside the hero with the new herd trail combing the meadow grass where a deer galloped; the lane is subtle and the hoof slots still vanish in the dark shaded soil under the grass.
The red deer herd, now with a stag, grazing the evening meadow under the mountains; the deer are small dark silhouettes at this range and the foreground grass is a dark wall.
The new red deer stag broadside with a royal crown of antlers and a dark rut mane beside a hind; the body is still a smooth, muscle-less loft and the oak crowns read stylized.
The stag now carries a deep chest under his rut neck and the hinds a tucked flank over a hanging thigh; at 8-12 m the deer still read as smooth, hairless shapes and the oak crowns stay stylized.
Model check of the sculpted stag: deep brisket, flank tuck, shoulder blade and haunch relief; the coat is still a noise texture with no hair cards and the head reads long and thin.
